newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean/Spanish financial group buys pension fund.
newsitem.headline: Chilean/Spanish financial group buys pension fund.

text.p: A Chilean/Spanish consortium formed by the local Luksic group and Banco Central Hispano has agreed to buy a stake in recently created private pension fund manager AFP Qualitas, said consortium officials.
The O'Higgins-Central Hispanoamericano group will buy 50.1 percent of Qualitas for 2.4 billion pesos, around $5.9 million, director Rodrigo Manubens told a news conference.
Qualitas was formed this week with the merger of two of pension funds Armoniza and Valora and will be Chile's 12th largest fund once the fusion is completed in November.
"We hope that Qualitas will be among the top funds in the pension system," said Manubens.
The consortium is one of the largest banking groups in the southern cone region with projects in Chile, Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay and Peru.
Its investments include controlling shareholdings in two of Chile's largest private banks, Banco O'Higgins and Banco de Santiago.
